why: Table 430.250 lists 14 A at 460 V; 28 A is the 230 V value.

q: What is the table full-load current of a 1 hp, 115 V, single-phase motor?
why: Table 430.248 lists 16 A at 115 V (8 A at 230 V).

q: Three 460 V motors draw 14 A, 21 A and 27 A. Minimum feeder conductor ampacity is:
A motor disconnect must be rated at least what percent of the motor FLC?
why: Motor disconnects must be rated at least 115% of full-load current.

q: A hermetic motor-compressor's SCGF protection normally may not exceed what percent of rated-load current?
why: 175% is the basic limit; 225% is allowed only if needed for starting.

q: A 120 V room air conditioner's cord may be no longer than:
why: 120 V room AC cords are limited to 10 ft; 208/240 V units to 6 ft.

q: Conductors from generator terminals to the first overcurrent device must have an ampacity of at least what percent of nameplate current?
why: 445.13 requires at least 115% of the generator nameplate current.

q: A transformer (1000 V or less) with primary-only protection and 90 A rated primary current may have a primary OCPD of at most:
why: 125% x 90 A = 112.5 A; the next higher standard size, 125 A, is permitted.

q: Indoor dry-type transformers 112.5 kVA or less must be separated from combustible material by at least:
why: 450.21(A) requires 12 in unless a fire-resistant, heat-insulating barrier is used. The rule does not apply to transformers of 1000 V or less that are completely enclosed except for ventilating openings.

q: Gasoline vapors are classified in which Class I group?
why: Gasoline, propane and natural gas are Group D; acetylene A, hydrogen B, ethylene C.

q: In a Class I, Division 1 location, a conduit seal must be within what distance of an explosionproof enclosure containing ignition sources?
why: Seals must be within 18 in of the enclosure; 10 ft is for boundary seals.

q: Combustible dust locations are which class?
why: Class II is combustible dust; Class I is gases/vapors; Class III is fibers/flyings.

q: How many receptacles are required at each critical care (Category 1) patient bed location?
why: Critical care bed locations need at least 14 receptacles; general care needs 8.

q: The pool equipotential bonding conductor must be at least:
why: 680.26(B) requires solid copper not smaller than 8 AWG.

q: Pool perimeter surfaces must be bonded for what distance beyond the inside walls of the pool?
why: Perimeter surfaces extending 3 ft horizontally beyond the inside walls must be bonded.

q: Under NEC 2023, receptacles rated 125-250 V and 60 A or less within what distance of a pool's inside walls require GFCI (or SPGFCI) protection?
why: 680.22(A)(4) requires GFCI (680.5(B)) or SPGFCI (680.5(C)) protection for these receptacles within 20 ft of the pool. NEC 2020 covered only 15/20 A, 125 V receptacles.

q: New outdoor luminaires within 5 ft horizontally of a pool must be at least how high above the maximum water level?
why: 680.22(B)(1) requires at least 12 ft above the maximum water level.

q: Pool water must be bonded with conductive surfaces totaling at least:
why: An intentional bond of at least 9 sq in in contact with the pool water is required.

q: Maximum PV system DC voltage on a one-family dwelling is:
why: One- and two-family dwellings are limited to 600 V DC; other buildings to 1000 V.

q: Outside the array boundary, PV rapid shutdown must reduce controlled conductors to no more than:
why: Outside the boundary: 30 V within 30 s; inside: 80 V within 30 s.

q: Emergency systems must provide power within how many seconds of normal power failure?
why: Emergency systems: 10 s. Legally required standby: 60 s.

q: Legally required standby systems must provide power within:
why: 701.12 allows up to 60 seconds; 10 seconds applies to emergency systems.

q: Emergency battery systems and unit equipment must carry the load for at least:
why: Batteries must supply the load for 1-1/2 hours (90 minutes) without dropping below 87.5% of voltage.

q: Overcurrent protection for an EV charger branch circuit must be rated at least what percent of the EVSE maximum load?
why: EVSE is a continuous load; OCPD is at least 125% of maximum load.

q: What is the voltage drop on a 120 V, 20 A single-phase circuit 100 ft one way using 12 AWG copper (K = 12.9, 6,530 cmil)?
What is the total resistance of a 6 ohm and a 3 ohm resistor in parallel?
why: (6 x 3) / (6 + 3) = 18 / 9 = 2 ohms; parallel total is less than the smallest branch.

q: A load uses 8 kW and 10 kVA. What is its power factor?
A 45 kVA balanced load at 208 V three-phase draws about:
why: 45,000 / (208 x 1.732) = about 125 A; 216 A would be single-phase math.

q: A 480:120 V transformer has 10 A on the primary. What is the secondary current?
why: A 4:1 step-down multiplies current by 4: 10 A x 4 = 40 A.

q: On a 120/240 V single-phase circuit, one leg carries 30 A and the other 20 A. Neutral current is:
why: The neutral carries the difference: 30 - 20 = 10 A.

q: In a 120/240 V high-leg delta system, the high leg measures about what voltage to neutral?
why: 120 V x 1.732 = about 208 V, so it cannot serve 120 V loads.

q: What is the synchronous speed of a 4-pole, 60 Hz motor?
On a construction site, OSHA requires GFCI protection (or an assured grounding program) for which temporary receptacles?
why: 1926.404(b)(1) covers 120 V, single-phase 15 and 20 A receptacles not part of permanent wiring.

q: Under an assured equipment grounding conductor program, routine tests are required at intervals not exceeding:
why: Tests are required every 3 months (6 months for fixed cords and receptacles not exposed to damage).

q: Hard-service flexible cords may be spliced/repaired only if they are at least:
why: Only hard-service cords 12 AWG or larger may be repaired, and the splice must keep the cord's properties.

q: An unqualified worker must stay at least how far from an energized overhead line of 50 kV or less?
why: 10 ft for 50 kV or less, plus 4 in per 10 kV above 50 kV.

q: Portable lighting used inside a metal tank must operate at 12 V or less unless it is:
why: 120 V lights may be used in wet/conductive locations only when GFCI protected.

q: OSHA requires lockout/tagout energy control procedures to be inspected at least:
why: Periodic inspections of energy control procedures are required at least annually.

q: Three 3 AWG copper THHN current-carrying conductors run through a rooftop space where the ambient is 54 C (129 F). What is the corrected ampacity?
why: Start with the 90 C value for 3 AWG copper (115 A) and multiply by the 51-55 C factor for 90 C conductors (0.76): 115 x 0.76 = 87.4 A.

q: With no clamps, devices or grounding conductors, how many 12 AWG conductors may go in a 4-11/16 x 2-1/8 in square metal box?
why: The box is 42.0 cu in and each 12 AWG needs 2.25 cu in: 42.0 / 2.25 = 18.7, so 18 conductors.

q: What minimum branch-circuit conductor ampacity is required for a 15 hp, 208 V, three-phase motor?
why: Table 430.250 gives 46.2 A for 15 hp at 208 V, and 430.22 requires 125%: 46.2 x 1.25 = 57.75 A.

q: How many 12 AWG THHN conductors are permitted in 1 in EMT (all the same size)?
why: 1 in EMT has 0.346 sq in at 40% fill; 0.346 / 0.0133 = 26.0, so 26 conductors.

q: A 20 hp, 230 V, 3-phase Design B motor (54 A table FLC) is on a circuit under 100 A. Using THHN copper, what is the smallest conductor allowed?
why: 54 x 1.25 = 68 A. Design B motors may use the 75 C column, where 6 AWG is only 65 A, so 4 AWG (85 A) is the minimum.

q: Six 3 AWG copper THHN current-carrying conductors share a raceway at 30 C, with 75 C terminals. What is their ampacity?
why: 115 A (90 C) x 0.80 for 4-6 conductors = 92 A, which is below the 100 A terminal limit, so 92 A applies.

q: Using Table 220.55 Column C, what is the maximum demand for 20 household ranges, each rated 12 kW?
why: Column C lists 35 kW for 20 ranges (15 kW plus 1 kW per range).

q: Fifteen ranges are rated 13 kW (5), 15 kW (5) and 17 kW (5). What is the Column C demand using Note 2?
why: The average is 15 kW, 3 kW over 12 kW, so increase the 15-range value (30 kW) by 15%: 30 x 1.15 = 34.5 kW.

q: A 2,400 sq ft house has a 12 kW range, a 5 kW dryer, 10 kW of electric heat and 6 kVA of AC. With the required small-appliance and laundry circuits, what is the standard-method load?
why: Lighting/SA/laundry 11,700 VA demands to 6,045 VA; add 8,000 (range), 5,000 (dryer) and 10,000 (heat, larger than AC) = 29,045 VA / 240 = about 121 A.

q: In the 220.82 optional method, a house has 33,200 VA of general loads and 5,000 VA of AC. What is the calculated load?
What is the minimum aluminum equipment grounding conductor for a feeder protected by a 400 A breaker?
why: Table 250.122 lists 1 AWG aluminum (3 AWG copper) for a 400 A device.

q: A feeder is protected by a 250 A breaker. What is the minimum copper EGC?
why: 250 A is not listed, so use the next larger row (300 A), which calls for 4 AWG copper.

q: A 2000 A feeder requires what minimum copper equipment grounding conductor in each raceway?
why: Table 250.122 lists 250 kcmil copper for 2000 A, and 250.122(F) requires a full-size EGC in each parallel raceway.

q: A service has two parallel sets of 250 kcmil copper per phase. What size copper GEC does Table 250.66 require (to a water pipe)?
why: Two 250 kcmil sets equal 500 kcmil per phase, which falls in the over 350 through 600 kcmil row: 1/0 copper.

q: What is the maximum inverse-time breaker for a 25 hp, 460 V, 3-phase motor, using the next-size-up rule?
why: FLC is 34 A; 34 x 250% = 85 A, which is not standard, so the next size up, 90 A, is allowed.

q: For a wound-rotor motor, the maximum inverse-time breaker rating (before exceptions) is what percent of FLC?
why: Table 430.52(C)(1) (Table 430.52 in NEC 2020) limits inverse-time breakers to 150% for wound-rotor motors; 250% applies to standard squirrel-cage motors.

q: A 3 hp, 208 V, 3-phase motor has 14 AWG copper conductors. What is the largest inverse-time breaker allowed?
why: FLC is 10.6 A; 10.6 x 2.5 = 26.5 A, next standard size 30 A. The 15 A limit of 240.4(D) does not apply to motor circuits.

q: A unit has an 18 A rated-load-current compressor and a 1.2 A fan. What minimum circuit ampacity is needed?
why: 125% of the compressor plus the fan: 18 x 1.25 + 1.2 = 23.7 A.

q: Equipment above a lay-in ceiling that may need servicing while energized must have an access opening of at least:
why: 110.26(A)(4) requires at least 22 x 22 in above a lay-in ceiling; 22 x 30 in is the crawl space minimum.

q: What is the minimum working space depth in front of a 208Y/120 V panelboard with exposed live parts across from a concrete wall (Condition 2)?
why: 208Y/120 V is 120 V to ground, in the 0-150 V row, which requires 3 ft for all three conditions.

q: A junction box feeding a wet-niche pool light (no barrier) must be at least how far from the inside wall of the pool?
why: 680.24(A)(2) requires the box to be at least 4 ft from the inside pool wall unless a solid fence, wall or permanent barrier separates them.

q: PV modules have a 35 V Voc. Using a 1.18 cold-temperature factor, what is the maximum voltage of 12 modules in series?
Emergency disconnects for gasoline dispensers must be located:
c: Within sight and not more than 50 ft away
At least 20 ft but not more than 100 ft from the dispensers
why: 514.11(A) requires emergency shutoffs at least 20 ft and no more than 100 ft from the dispensers they serve.

q: Two 100 W, 120 V lamps are connected in series across 120 V. How much power does each lamp use?
why: Each lamp is 144 ohms; in series the current is 120 / 288 = 0.417 A, so each lamp uses 0.417 squared x 144 = 25 W.

q: Two 50 kVA single-phase transformers are connected open delta. About how much 3-phase load can they supply?
why: Open delta delivers 86.6% of the two units' combined rating: 100 kVA x 0.866 = 86.6 kVA.

q: A 100 kW load runs at 0.80 power factor. About how many kVAR of capacitors raise it to 0.95 PF?
why: At 0.80 PF the load has 75 kVAR; at 0.95 PF it has about 32.9 kVAR; 75 - 32.9 = about 42 kVAR.

q: Which location was ADDED to the tamper-resistant receptacle requirement in NEC 2023?
why: Fitness centers (along with nursing homes and similar facilities) were added in 2023; the other choices were already covered.

q: A box holds four 12 AWG and two 14 AWG insulated conductors, internal clamps, one receptacle connected to 12 AWG, and the EGCs (12 AWG largest). What volume is required?
why: 4 x 2.25 + 2 x 2.00 = 13.0; clamps 2.25; device 2 x 2.25 = 4.5; grounds 2.25. Total = 22.0 cu in.

q: A box is 30.3 cu in and has a plaster ring marked 3.6 cu in. What volume may be used for the box fill calculation?
why: Marked volumes of plaster rings, extension rings and domed covers are added to the box volume: 30.3 + 3.6 = 33.9 cu in.

q: Three 4 AWG THHN conductors and one bare stranded 8 AWG EGC need what minimum size EMT?
why: 3 x 0.0824 + 0.017 = 0.2642 sq in. 3/4 in EMT allows 0.213 sq in at 40%; 1 in EMT allows 0.346 sq in, so 1 in is needed.

q: A pull box has a U pull with two 3 in conduits (4/0 conductors) entering the same wall. What is the minimum distance to the opposite wall?
why: For angle and U pulls: 6 x the largest raceway plus the other raceways on that wall: 6 x 3 + 3 = 21 in.

q: 250 kcmil copper conductors in a vertical raceway must be supported at intervals not exceeding:
why: Table 300.19(A) allows 60 ft for copper over 4/0 through 350 kcmil.

q: Temporary wiring for holiday decorative lighting may remain in place for no more than:
why: 590.3(B) limits holiday and similar decorative temporary lighting to 90 days.

q: The patient care vicinity extends how far horizontally beyond the normal location of the patient bed?
why: The patient care vicinity extends 6 ft beyond the bed and 7 ft 6 in above the floor.

q: What is the ambient temperature correction factor for a 90 C conductor in a 73 C (163 F) space?
why: Table 310.15(B)(1)(1) gives 0.50 for 71-75 C in the 90 C column; 0.58 is for 66-70 C.

q: With nothing else in the box, how many 14 AWG conductors may be installed in a 4 x 1-1/2 in square metal box?
why: The box is 21.0 cu in; 21.0 / 2.00 = 10.5, so 10 conductors of 14 AWG.

q: A feeder has a 300 A calculated load. What is the smallest aluminum conductor (75 C column, no derating) with enough ampacity?
why: At 75 C, aluminum 350 kcmil is 250 A and 400 kcmil is 270 A; 500 kcmil is 310 A, the first size at or above 300 A.

q: What minimum conductor ampacity is required for a 5 hp, 230 V, single-phase motor?
why: Table 430.248 lists 28 A for 5 hp at 230 V; 28 x 1.25 = 35 A.

q: What is the minimum aluminum EGC for a circuit protected by a 1200 A overcurrent device?
why: Table 250.122 lists 250 kcmil aluminum (3/0 copper) for 1200 A.

q: An EV charger requires a readily accessible disconnecting means when it is rated more than:
why: 625.43 requires a readily accessible disconnect for EVSE rated more than 60 A (or more than 150 V to ground).

q: In an existing dwelling, a 200 A panelboard is being replaced in a basement with 6 ft 2 in of headroom. Does 110.26 allow it?
c: No, 6-1/2 ft headroom is always required
Only with a written variance from the utility
Only if the panel is 100 A or less
Yes, existing dwelling equipment rated 200 A or less is exempt from the height rule
why: 110.26(A)(3) Exception No. 2 exempts service equipment and panelboards rated 200 A or less in existing dwelling units from the 6-1/2 ft height requirement.

q: At a gasoline dispenser, where must the conduit seal be located?
c: Within 18 in of the dispenser enclosure
As the first fitting after the conduit emerges from the earth or concrete
why: 514.9(A) requires the seal (or listed explosionproof reducer) to be the first fitting after the raceway emerges from earth or concrete.

q: A 50 kVA single-phase transformer has a 480 V primary and primary-only protection. What is the maximum standard primary OCPD?
why: 50,000 / 480 = 104.2 A; x 1.25 = 130.2 A. Note 1 allows the next higher standard size, 150 A.

q: Ten 5 kW cooktops (Column B) are installed. What is their demand load using Table 220.55 Column B?
why: Column B gives 34% for 10 appliances: 50 kW x 0.34 = 17 kW.

q: Four 14/2 NM cables pass through one bored hole that will be sealed with fire caulk. What is the maximum ampacity of each conductor?
why: Eight current-carrying conductors take a 70% factor: 25 A (90 C) x 0.70 = 17.5 A, but NM cable is limited to the 60 C value of 15 A.

q: Under the 2021 IRC, what is the minimum clear width of a stairway above the permitted handrail height?
why: R311.7.1 requires stairways to be at least 36 in clear above the handrail height; 44 in is the common IBC egress stair width.

q: Under the 2021 IRC, a nosing is not required on a stair when the tread depth is at least:
why: Nosings of 3/4 to 1-1/4 in are required on solid-riser stairs unless the tread depth is 11 in or more.

q: Under the 2021 IRC, a guard is required where an open-sided deck is more than how high above the grade below (measured within 36 in of the edge)?
why: Guards are required where the walking surface is more than 30 in above the floor or grade within 36 in horizontally of the open side.

q: What is the minimum required guard height for a deck in a one-family dwelling under the model 2021 IRC?
why: R312.1.2 requires 36 in guards; 34 in applies to guards along the open sides of stairs, and 42 in is the IBC (and some state) requirement.

q: Guards on the open side of an IRC stairway may not have openings that pass a sphere of what diameter?
why: The general guard limit is a 4 in sphere, but the open side of stairs is allowed 4-3/8 in; the 6 in sphere applies only to the riser/tread/bottom rail triangle.

q: Under the 2021 IRC, window fall protection is required when the bottom of an operable window's clear opening is less than 24 in above the floor and more than how high above the grade outside?
why: R312.2.1 applies where the bottom of the clear opening is under 24 in above the finished floor and more than 72 in above the finished grade or surface below.

q: What is the minimum net clear opening for an emergency escape window on a second-floor bedroom under the 2021 IRC?
why: Escape openings need at least 5.7 sq ft; the 5.0 sq ft allowance is only for grade-floor openings.

q: A window well serving a basement escape window needs a permanently attached ladder or steps when the well is deeper than:
why: Area wells deeper than 44 in require a permanent ladder or steps that can be used with the window fully open.

q: Which window pane requires safety glazing under IRC R308.4.3?
c: 10 sq ft pane, bottom edge 16 in above floor, top edge 70 in, walkway 24 in away
8 sq ft pane, bottom edge 12 in above floor, top edge 60 in, walkway 24 in away
12 sq ft pane, bottom edge 20 in above floor, top edge 80 in, walkway 24 in away
12 sq ft pane, bottom edge 12 in above floor, top edge 80 in, walkway 48 in away
why: All four conditions must be met: over 9 sq ft, bottom under 18 in, top over 36 in, and a walking surface within 36 in. Each wrong choice misses one condition.

q: What is the minimum horizontal distance between an ionization smoke alarm without a silencing switch and a permanently installed cooking appliance?
why: R314.3.1 keeps ionization alarms at least 20 ft from a permanently installed cooking appliance (10 ft with a silencing switch); photoelectric alarms need 6 ft.

q: Under the 2021 IRC, which new all-electric home is required to have carbon monoxide alarms?
c: One heated by an electric heat pump
One with an attached garage that has a door into the house
why: CO alarms are required where there is a fuel-fired appliance or an attached garage with an opening into the dwelling.

q: Under the IRC, what must separate a garage from a habitable room located above it?
c: 1/2 in regular gypsum board on the garage side
why: Table R302.6 requires at least 5/8 in Type X gypsum board between a garage and habitable rooms above; 1/2 in board is enough for walls between the garage and the house.

q: A house without sprinklers has an exterior wall 4 ft from the lot line. Under Table R302.1(1), how much of that wall may be openings?
why: Openings are not allowed under 3 ft, limited to 25 percent of the wall area from 3 ft to under 5 ft, and unlimited at 5 ft or more.

q: What is the minimum thickness of a concrete spread footing under IRC R403.1.1?
why: Footings must be at least 6 in thick and 12 in wide, with a projection of at least 2 in but not more than the footing thickness.

q: A stud in an exterior bearing wall may be notched to a maximum depth of what percent of its width?
why: Bearing studs may be notched 25 percent; nonbearing studs 40 percent; bored holes may be up to 60 percent of the width.

q: An office floor of 15,000 gross sq ft is used as business space. What is its occupant load under 2021 IBC Table 1004.5?
why: Business areas use 150 gross sq ft per occupant: 15,000 / 150 = 100 occupants.

q: A banquet hall has 3,000 net sq ft set with tables and chairs. What is its occupant load?
why: Unconcentrated assembly (tables and chairs) uses 15 net sq ft per person: 3,000 / 15 = 200. 429 would be the chairs-only factor of 7, and 600 the standing factor of 5.

q: What is the maximum exit access travel distance in a fully sprinklered Group B building under the 2021 IBC?
why: Group B allows 200 ft without sprinklers and 300 ft with sprinklers; 250 ft applies to sprinklered A, E, F-1, M, R and S-1.

q: A story has an occupant load of 750. What is the minimum number of exits required from that story?
why: Two exits serve 1-500 occupants, three serve 501-1,000, and four are needed above 1,000.

q: What is the minimum corridor width for a corridor serving 120 occupants in an office building under the 2021 IBC?
why: The general minimum is 44 in; 36 in applies only with fewer than 50 occupants, and 72 in is for Group E corridors serving 100 or more.

q: Under IBC Table 601, what fire-resistance rating is required for the primary structural frame of Type IA construction?
why: Type IA requires a 3-hour primary structural frame; Type IB requires 2 hours.

q: Under the 2021 IBC, a Group A-2 restaurant must be sprinklered when its fire area exceeds:
why: A-2 occupancies need sprinklers over 5,000 sq ft, with 100 or more occupants, or on a floor other than the exit discharge level.

q: An assisted living facility provides 24-hour custodial care to 20 residents. What is its IBC occupancy classification?
why: R-4 covers more than 5 but not more than 16 residents; more than 16 residents in custodial care is Group I-1.

q: What minimum fire protection rating is required for a door in a 2-hour fire barrier?
why: Table 716.1(2) requires 1-1/2-hour doors in 2-hour fire walls and fire barriers; 1-hour shaft and exit enclosures need 1-hour doors.

q: A parking lot has 120 total spaces. How many accessible spaces does the 2010 ADA Standards require?
why: 101-150 total spaces require 5 accessible spaces, and at least one of them must be van accessible.

q: Under ACI 318, when f'c is 4,000 psi, no individual strength test may fall below f'c by more than:
why: For f'c of 5,000 psi or less, no single test may be more than 500 psi low, and every average of three consecutive tests must reach f'c.

q: Which ASTM C270 mortar type has a minimum compressive strength of 1,800 psi?
why: Type M is 2,500 psi, Type S 1,800 psi, Type N 750 psi and Type O 350 psi.

q: Where an ice barrier is required by the IRC, it must extend from the lowest roof edge to a point at least how far inside the exterior wall line?
why: The ice barrier extends at least 24 in inside the exterior wall line; on roofs 8:12 or steeper it must also run at least 36 in up the slope.

q: About how many modular brick are needed for 400 sq ft of wall with 3/8-in joints, before waste?
why: Modular brick runs about 6.75 per sq ft: 400 x 6.75 = 2,700 brick.

q: A roof has 2,000 sq ft of plan area and a 6:12 slope (slope factor 1.118). About how many squares of roofing does it need before waste?
why: Roof area = 2,000 x 1.118 = 2,236 sq ft, and one square is 100 sq ft, so about 22.4 squares.

q: Under the Miller Act, a supplier to a subcontractor must give the prime contractor written notice of its claim within how many days after its last delivery?
why: Second-tier claimants must give written notice to the prime within 90 days of their last labor or material.

q: What is the deadline to file a Miller Act payment bond lawsuit?
c: 90 days after last labor or material
1 year after last labor or material
why: Suit must be filed no later than one year after the claimant last performed labor or supplied material, in federal district court.

q: On a federal fixed-price construction contract, when may the contracting officer hold back retainage, and how much?
c: Only if progress is unsatisfactory, up to 10 percent
Only on the final payment, up to 20 percent
why: FAR 52.232-5(e) requires full payment when progress is satisfactory; up to 10 percent may be retained only when it is not.

q: Under the federal Changes clause, a contractor cannot recover costs of a constructive change incurred more than how many days before it gave written notice?
why: Costs incurred more than 20 days before written notice are not recoverable (except for defective specifications); the 30-day rule is for asserting the adjustment.

q: Which describes a Type I differing site condition?
c: Extra work ordered orally by the owner
Subsurface or hidden conditions that differ materially from those shown in the contract
Unknown unusual conditions that differ from those ordinarily encountered
why: Type I is a material difference from what the contract indicates; Type II is an unusual condition that differs from what is normally encountered.

q: Which AIA document is the owner-contractor agreement for the cost of the work plus a fee with a guaranteed maximum price?
why: A101 is stipulated sum, A102 is cost plus fee with a GMP, A103 is cost plus fee without a GMP, and A201 is the general conditions.

q: Under AIA A201-2017, if the owner fails to pay within seven days after the payment due date, the contractor may stop work after giving how many additional days' written notice?
why: Section 9.7 lets the contractor stop work on seven additional days' notice and recover reasonable shutdown, delay and start-up costs.

q: A subcontractor is about to receive a progress check it has not yet been paid. Which lien waiver should it sign?
why: A conditional progress waiver takes effect only if the progress payment is actually received; unconditional waivers are for payments already received.

q: To be exempt from overtime under the FLSA white-collar exemptions, an employee must pass the duties test and be paid a salary of at least:
why: The 2026 DOL rule rescinded the 2024 increases, leaving the threshold at $684 per week ($35,568 a year).

q: An employer enrolled in E-Verify must create the E-Verify case for a new hire no later than:
c: Before the job offer is made
The employee's first day of work
The third business day after the employee starts work for pay
why: Form I-9 is completed first, and the E-Verify case must be created by the third business day after the employee starts work for pay.

q: When is Form 941 for January through March due?
why: Form 941 is due the last day of the month after the quarter ends (April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31), with 10 extra days if all deposits were on time.

q: A subcontractor refuses to provide its taxpayer identification number on Form W-9. At what rate must the payer apply backup withholding?
why: The current backup withholding rate is 24 percent.

q: A contractor has total liabilities of $450,000 and owner's equity of $300,000. What is its debt-to-equity ratio?
why: Debt-to-equity = total liabilities / owner's equity = $450,000 / $300,000 = 1.5.

q: A $1,000,000 contract has $600,000 of costs to date and $800,000 of total estimated costs. Using cost-to-cost percentage of completion, what is the earned revenue?
why: Percent complete = $600,000 / $800,000 = 75 percent, and 75 percent of $1,000,000 = $750,000 earned.

q: A worker dies from injuries 45 days after a work-related incident. Must the employer report the death to OSHA?
c: No, a fatality is reportable only if it occurs within 30 days of the incident
No, fatalities are only recorded on the 300 log after 7 days
Yes, within 8 hours of learning of it
why: Fatalities must be reported within 8 hours only if the death occurs within 30 days of the work-related incident; the case is still recorded on the 300 log.

q: Which edition of the National Electrical Code did Nebraska's State Electrical Division adopt effective August 1, 2024?
why: Nebraska adopted the 2023 NEC (NFPA 70) starting August 1, 2024, and PSI exams moved to the 2023 code that day.

q: How much verifiable experience does Nebraska require for a journeyman electrician license?
why: Nebraska requires at least four years (8,000 hours) of verifiable electrical experience for the journeyman license.

q: Which plumbing code is part of Nebraska's state building code under Neb. Rev. Stat. 71-6403?
why: The Nebraska state building code adopts the 2018 Uniform Plumbing Code along with the 2018 IBC, IRC and IEBC.

q: In Nevada, which State Contractors Board classification covers refrigeration and air-conditioning contracting?
why: Classification C-21 is refrigeration and air-conditioning, with subclassifications C-21a through C-21g.

q: How much trade experience does Nevada require of a contractor license's trade qualified individual?
why: The NSCB requires at least 4 years of experience in the trade, gained within the past 15 years.

q: Since July 1, 2025, which NEC edition is part of the New Hampshire state building code?
why: HB 134 (2025 Laws ch. 135) changed the state building code from the 2020 to the 2023 NEC effective July 1, 2025.

q: Which plumbing code does New Jersey adopt in its Uniform Construction Code plumbing subcode?
c: A New Jersey plumbing code with no model code base
why: New Jersey's plumbing subcode adopts the National Standard Plumbing Code (2024, NJ edition), not the IPC or UPC.

q: The New Jersey electrical contractor exam has three parts. Which list is correct?
c: Trade, alarm systems, and business and law
Business and law, OSHA, and load calculations
Trade, fire sprinklers, and energy code
why: The NJ Board says the exam covers electrical contractor (trade), alarm systems, and business and law.

q: Which model plumbing code does New Mexico adopt for its state plumbing code (14.8.2 NMAC)?
why: The 2024 New Mexico Plumbing Code (14.8.2 NMAC, effective August 1, 2026) adopts the 2024 Uniform Plumbing Code with state amendments. It replaced the 2021 New Mexico Plumbing Code, which was also UPC-based.

q: Since August 1, 2026, which New Mexico mechanical classification covers HVAC, hydronics, fuel gas piping and process piping?
why: MM-3 is HVAC, hydronics, fuel gas piping and process piping. MM-1 is plumbing and fuel gas piping, MM-98 combines MM-1 and MM-3, EE-98 is electrical and GB-98 is general building. MM-2 and MM-4 were eliminated on August 1, 2026.

q: A New York City master electrician applicant generally needs how much experience under a licensed master or special electrician?
ref: NYC DOB Master Electrician License page
why: NYC DOB requires at least 7 years of experience within the 10 years before applying, with at least 2 years in NYC.

q: When did the 2025 New York State Uniform Code, including the 2025 Plumbing Code of NYS, take effect?
why: The 2025 Uniform Code took effect December 31, 2025, after a transition period from October 1 to December 30, 2025.

q: As of 2026, North Carolina's State Electrical Code for commercial and multifamily buildings (everything except one- and two-family dwellings) is based on which NEC edition?
ref: NC OSFM State Electrical Code page
why: The 2020 NC State Electrical Code (2020 NEC with amendments) has applied since November 1, 2021, except to one- and two-family dwellings, which still use the 2017 NC State Electrical Code. The 2023 code was delayed indefinitely by S.L. 2025-2.

q: How many hours of experience does an Unlimited electrical contractor exam applicant need in North Carolina?
why: Unlimited applicants need 9,000 hours (at least 8,000 primary). Limited needs 3,000, and Intermediate needs 5,750.

q: Effective July 1, 2026, which NEC edition do North Dakota's State Electrical Board wiring standards adopt?
why: The ND wiring standards now name the NFPA 70 2026 edition, effective July 1, 2026. The state was on the 2023 NEC from July 1, 2024.

q: Which code is the North Dakota state plumbing code based on?
why: The State Plumbing Board adopts the 2018 UPC as the 2018 North Dakota Plumbing Code.

q: The 2024 Ohio Plumbing Code, effective March 1, 2024, is based on which model code?
why: Ohio adopted the 2021 IPC (with Ohio changes) as the 2024 Ohio Plumbing Code, effective March 1, 2024.

q: Under Ohio Rev. Code 4740.06, how many years as a tradesperson must an OCILB exam applicant normally have right before applying?
why: Ohio requires at least five years as a tradesperson in that trade immediately before applying, or three years for an Ohio-registered engineer.

q: Effective September 14, 2026, which plumbing code edition is Oklahoma's statewide minimum?
why: The OUBCC adopted the 2024 IPC effective September 14, 2026, replacing the 2018 IPC. Oklahoma never adopted the 2021 IPC.

q: How much plumbing experience does Oklahoma's CIB require for a plumbing journeyman license?
why: A plumbing journeyman needs three years of experience while employed by a licensed plumbing contractor. A contractor needs one more year.

q: Under Oklahoma's CIB rules, the HVAC Limited mechanical journeyman category covers cooling equipment up to how many tons?
why: HVAC Limited covers cooling up to 25 tons and heating up to 500,000 Btu/h per appliance. HVAC Unlimited has no capacity cap.

q: Which model code is the 2026 Oregon Plumbing Specialty Code based on?
why: The 2026 OPSC, effective October 1, 2026, is based on the 2024 UPC. The 2023 OPSC was based on the 2021 UPC.

q: Which NEC edition is the 2026 Oregon Electrical Specialty Code based on?
why: The 2026 OESC is based on the 2026 NEC and took effect October 1, 2026.

q: An Oregon General Supervising Electrician (S) applicant must hold a journeyman license (or its qualifications) plus how many more hours of journeyman experience?
why: The S license requires verification of an additional 8,000 hours of on-the-job journeyman experience.

q: Since January 1, 2026, which plumbing code does Pennsylvania's statewide Uniform Construction Code use?
c: Pennsylvania has no statewide plumbing code
ref: Phila. L&I Bulletin B-2501; City of York
why: Pennsylvania's UCC moved from the 2018 to the 2021 International Codes, including the 2021 IPC, on January 1, 2026.

q: Which NEC edition is referenced under Pennsylvania's 2021 Uniform Construction Code (effective January 1, 2026)?
ref: Phila. L&I Bulletin B-2501; City of York
why: Both Philadelphia L&I and the City of York list the 2020 NFPA 70 as the electrical standard under the 2021 UCC.

q: Which plumbing code does Rhode Island adopt as RISBC-3?
why: RISBC-3 adopts the 2021 IPC; the current version of the rule took effect December 1, 2025.

q: To take Rhode Island's Class A electrical contractor exam, how long must the applicant have held a Rhode Island journeyperson license?
why: The journeyperson license must be valid at least two years before applying, with six years of total trade experience.

q: In Rhode Island, a mechanical master license holder may do the sheet metal work without a separate license when the AC air handling equipment is no more than:
why: The exception covers AC air handling equipment of 10 tons or less or heating equipment of 250,000 BTU or less.

q: Which NEC edition has been mandatory statewide in South Carolina since January 1, 2023?
why: The SC Building Codes Council adopted the 2020 NEC (with SC changes) on October 6, 2021, effective January 1, 2023.

q: In South Carolina, residential HVAC work over what amount requires a Residential HVAC license?
ref: SC LLR Residential HVAC License page
why: Residential HVAC work over $500 needs the license. Commercial HVAC work over $10,000 falls under the Contractor's Licensing Board.

q: Under SDCL 36-25-15, plumbing in South Dakota must substantially conform to which code?
why: SB 25 (2025) moved South Dakota from the 2015 UPC to the 2024 UPC, and cities may not substitute another plumbing code.

q: Which NEC edition is Tennessee's statewide electrical code under State Fire Marshal rule 0780-02-01-.02?
why: Tennessee still uses the 2017 NEC (adopted in 2018). Its plumbing, mechanical and fuel gas codes moved to 2021 editions in April 2025.

q: Which plumbing code edition did Tennessee's State Fire Marshal's Office adopt effective April 17, 2025?
why: The SFMO adopted the 2021 IPC (along with the 2021 IMC, IFGC and IBC) effective April 17, 2025.

q: Effective September 1, 2026, which NEC edition did TDLR adopt as the Texas state electrical code?
why: TDLR adopted the 2026 NEC effective September 1, 2026, replacing the 2023 NEC that took effect September 1, 2023.

q: Which plumbing codes does the Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners adopt by rule (22 TAC 367.2)?
c: Both the Uniform Plumbing Code and the International Plumbing Code
why: TSBPE adopts both the Uniform Plumbing Code and the International Plumbing Code by rule, and plumbing in areas with no local code must follow one of them. The rule has used the 2018 editions, and a 2026 proposal would move it to the 2021 editions.

q: Effective September 1, 2026, TDLR's air conditioning and refrigeration rules reference which editions of the IMC and UMC?
why: TDLR updated the ACR rules from the 2021 to the 2024 IRC, IMC, IFGC and UMC effective September 1, 2026.

q: Which NEC edition does Utah's State Construction Code (Utah Code 15A-2-103) adopt?
why: Utah Code 15A-2-103 adopts the 2023 NEC (effective July 1, 2025), along with the 2024 IBC, IPC, IMC and IFGC and the 2021 IRC. Homes built under the IRC follow the IRC's electrical chapters instead (15A-3-601).

q: Under Utah Code 58-55-302, a master plumber who qualifies through the journeyman path must have been a licensed journeyman plumber for at least:
why: The journeyman path requires at least two years as a licensed journeyman plus two years of supervisory experience.

q: Which Utah contractor classification covers complete warm-air heating, air conditioning and ventilating systems?
why: S350 is the HVAC Contractor classification. E200 is general electrical, P200 is general plumbing, and B100 is general building.

q: Which model plumbing code is the base for Vermont's plumbing code, together with the 2025 Vermont Plumbing Rules?
why: Vermont DFS lists the 2024 IPC with the 2025 Vermont Plumbing Rules as the state plumbing code.

q: Which NEC edition is part of Virginia's 2021 Uniform Statewide Building Code (effective January 18, 2024)?
ref: Virginia DHCD Building and Fire Codes
why: DHCD says Virginia adopted the 2020 NEC with the 2021 codes, effective January 18, 2024.

q: In Virginia, an applicant with 240 hours of vocational training needs how many years of experience for a journeyman tradesman exam?
why: 240 hours of vocational training pairs with 4 years of experience. With no training, 8 years is required.

q: Which plumbing code does Washington State adopt in WAC 51-56?
c: Washington Plumbing Code with no model base
why: Washington adopts the 2021 Uniform Plumbing Code as its state plumbing code, effective March 15, 2024.

q: When does the 2026 NEC take effect under Washington's electrical rules (WAC 296-46B)?
why: L&I adopted the 2026 NEC with a delayed effective date of December 31, 2026. The 2023 NEC took effect April 1, 2024.

q: How many hours of experience are required for Washington's 06A HVAC/refrigeration specialty electrician certificate?
why: The 06A certificate requires 4,000 hours. The 06B restricted certificate requires 2,000 hours.

q: West Virginia electrical license exams are open book and based on which NEC edition?
ref: WV State Fire Marshal Electrical Licensing
why: The WV State Fire Marshal says all electrical exams are based solely on the 2020 NEC.

q: How many hours of HVAC work, training and experience does West Virginia require for an HVAC Technician certification?
ref: WV Division of Labor HVAC Certification
why: An HVAC Technician needs at least 2,000 hours. A Technician in Training must work under an HVAC Technician's direct supervision.

q: Effective September 1, 2026, Wisconsin's electrical code is based on which NEC edition?
why: Wisconsin moved from the 2017 NEC to the 2023 NEC (with state changes) on September 1, 2026.

q: Wisconsin's HVAC Qualifier certification requires 4 years of HVAC experience with at least how many hours per year?
why: The experience route requires at least 4 years at 1,000 hours per year, or 4 years of approved schooling, or a mix.

q: Which mechanical code edition did Wyoming adopt on June 28, 2024?
ref: Wyoming State Fire Marshal Rules and Statutes
why: Wyoming adopted the 2024 International Codes, including the 2024 IMC and IFGC, on June 28, 2024.

q: How many trainee hours does Washington require for a journey level plumber (PL01) certificate?
why: PL01 requires at least 8,000 hours (four years) as a trainee, including at least 4,000 commercial or industrial hours.

q: Since September 1, 2025, how long must a Texas journeyman plumber without a DOL-approved apprenticeship program hold the journeyman license to qualify for the master plumber exam?
ref: TSBPE Master Plumber page; TSBPE notice
why: TSBPE cut the standard requirement from four years to two years as a licensed journeyman, effective September 1, 2025. With a DOL Office of Apprenticeship-approved program, one year is enough.

q: Which is one way to qualify for a Wisconsin master electrician license?
c: Passing the exam with no experience
why: Wisconsin accepts 12 months as a licensed journeyman, 10,000 hours over 60 months, or an electrical engineering degree.
